messages.subject: Fwd: Seasonality in "setar()" and "star()"
messages.body_plain:
Hi

No, it is unfortunately not possible to supply exogeneous variables in lstar() nor in setar(). In setar you could eventually specify seasonal lags (-24 h, -7 days...), with the ML, MH arguments. Or simply resort to do first "de-seasonalalisation filtering".

CCing to the tsDyn mailing list for the record.

Best

Matthieu

messages.subject: Re: Can "seasonal STAR" model fit into the function"predict{tsDyn}"?
messages.subject_clean: Can "seasonal STAR" model fit into the function"predict{tsDyn}"?
messages.body_plain:
Hi

As discussed previously in a similar post, tsDyn does not allow for exogeneous regressors, see:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/tsdyn/ts-FZgL6D8E

If you were to modify lstar() yourself, you should modify several lines, the most important being 85 and 86:
xxL <- cbind(const,xx[,1:mL])

then add your regressors. YOu will need probably to modify the code at several other places, to take into account the fact that you have more regressors, hence parameter naming might fail. You will in any case not be able to use the predict() since the predict use a loop starting from zero to re-create the series. This would require significant changes.

Good luck

PS: copying to the mailing list for archiving, and to Anzor who asked a similar question.

Matthieu
